result.title: What Breaks in Multi-Image Schema Application? Factorial Oracle Interventions Reveal an Instance-Information Bottleneck
result.summary: Modern vision-language models can accept multi-image contexts, but aggregate accuracy rarely reveals where a multi-image reasoning pipeline fails. We study a controlled schema-application task in which a model must locate two target characters in a 16-image sequence, identify their visual attributes, consult an item-specific visual codebook, and compose two ordered nonce code names. We introduce a within-item 2-by-2 factorial Oracle design: Oracle-A supplies a verified textual schema, Oracle-B supplies a verified ordered target-appearance representation, and both interventions retain the original images and final question. Across 72 new items and 1,188 analyzed model responses, Oracle-B increased strict exact accuracy by 54.6 percentage points (95% confidence interval: 46.3 to 63.0) and outperformed Oracle-A by 60.6 points (Holm-adjusted p-value no greater than .0002). An auxiliary retrieval diagnostic reached only 49.1% ordered-appearance accuracy even after removing code-name generation. Providing both Oracle sources yielded 100% accuracy across all models. These results localize the dominant recoverable deficit to upstream ordered instance recovery rather than primarily to downstream schema use and composition.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建一个受控的多图 schema 应用任务（在 16 张图中定位两个目标字符、读取视觉属性、查物品专属 codebook 并合成有序代号），用 within-item 2×2 Oracle 干预（提供已验证文本 schema 或有序目标外观表示）分析 72 个条目、1188 条回答，定位多图流程的主要失败环节。
AI.relevance_reason: 材料支持的 Oracle-B 增益远超 Oracle-A，说明瓶颈在「有序实例信息恢复」这一上游环节，直接关联 LVR 关注的视觉细节与实体信息是否保留在内部状态、以及贡献分配诊断；其 Oracle 因子设计可供核查是否可迁移为 latent 内容因果归因工具，但任务为合成 codebook 场景，外推需谨慎。
